cohort: The study included full-term pregnant women without associated pathology who received acupuncture for labor induction at the Provincial Gyneco-obstetric Teaching Hospital Jose Ramon Lopez Tabrane, Matanzas.
finding: The application of acupuncture for labor induction was found to be satisfactory, with a higher frequency of patients experiencing a contractile response within 12 hours, labor up to six hours, and eutocic delivery; however, a contractile response in 21-36 hours increased the risk of adverse events including instrumental delivery, perinatal asphyxia, cesarean section, bleeding, and maternal sepsis.
mod_finding: Eutocic delivery was a frequent outcome, but an increased risk of instrumental delivery and cesarean section was observed when the contractile response occurred 21-36 hours after acupuncture.
